definition.def: A route is a way from one place to another.
examples: ...the most direct route to the town centre.
All escape routes were blocked by armed police.
Tens of thousands lined the route from Dublin airport.

definition.def: A bus, air, or shipping route is the way between two places along which buses, planes, or ships travel regularly.
In the United States, Route is used in front of a number in the names of main roads between major cities.
Your route is the series of visits you make to different people or places, as part of your job. [mainly US]
examples: He began cracking open big blue tins of butter cookies and feeding the dogs on his route.
They would go out on his route and check him.

definition.def: You can refer to a way of achieving something as a route.
examples: Researchers are trying to get at the same information through an indirect route.
Buying the best is as sure a route to success in investment as in any other field.

definition.def: If vehicles, goods, or passengers are routed in a particular direction, they are made to travel in that direction.
examples: Double-stack trains are taking a lot of freight that used to be routed via trucks. [be VERB-ed preposition/adverb]
Approaching cars will be routed into two lanes. [be VERB-ed preposition/adverb]

definition.def: If phone calls or other electronic signals are routed in a particular way, the signals are sent through a particular series of connections. [technical]
examples: ...plans to route every emergency call in the country through just three telephone exchanges. [VERB noun preposition/adverb]

definition.def: Journalists sometimes use en route when they are mentioning an event that happened as part of a longer process or before another event.
examples: The German set three tournament records en route to grabbing golf's richest prize. [+ to]

definition.def: En route to a place means on the way to that place. En route is sometimes spelled on route in non-standard English.
examples: They have arrived in London en route to the United States. [+ to]
One of the bags was lost en route.

definition.def: If you go the route, you do something fully or continue with a task until you have completely finished. [US]
examples: Health enthusiasts like myself want to go the route of prevention rather than cure.
